images.edition: Correspondentie van Willem III en van Hans Willem Bentinck, eerste gedeelte, deel 2, KS 24
images.content: Alphabetische lijst van brieven -- the Vaudemont correspondent index, listing every letter by date with an asterisk marking cipher letters; the 25 March 1699 entry carries the note 'grootendeels in onopgelost cijferschrift; ook een ontcijferde brief is aanwezig'

images.edition: Correspondentie van Willem III en van Hans Willem Bentinck, eerste gedeelte, deel 2, KS 24
images.content: Letter no. 32 (Sunderland to Willem III, 20 June 1693), footnote 1: 'De gespatieerd gedrukte woorden zijn in den brief uit cijferschrift opgelost' -- the edition's general statement that letter-spaced type marks a passage decoded from cipher. Fetched to confirm the convention seen at p.242 is house style, not specific to Vaudemont.

images.edition: Correspondentie van Willem III en van Hans Willem Bentinck, eerste gedeelte, deel 2, KS 24
images.content: Letter no. 219 (Vaudemont, 18 March 1699, 'met bijlage'): ordinary plain French, not cipher. Closing lines are the first mention of a shared cipher between Vaudemont and Bentinck ('nous avons un chifre').

images.edition: Correspondentie van Willem III en van Hans Willem Bentinck, eerste gedeelte, deel 2, KS 24
images.content: Letter no. 220 (Vaudemont, *25 March 1699, the target). A middle passage is printed in letter-spaced type; footnote 1 states the letter survives mostly in cipher and that a solved exemplaar in Robethon's hand also exists, which Japikse follows in the text. This is the edition's own resolution of the p.812 index's 'ook een ontcijferde brief is aanwezig'.

No archive shelfmark or inventory number is given anywhere in this edition for the 25 March 1699 letter or its Robethon-hand decipherment exemplaar; both are held in the Portland (Welbeck) collection, University of Nottingham (not Nationaal Archief 3.01.19), per CLAUDE.md's Access playbook -- not copy-free.
